terms.gloss: so be it, as you please
terms.grammar: estō, future imperative of sum, “let it be”; ut lubet (libet), “as it pleases”
terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase, made of two classical pieces: estō, granting a point (Plaut., Cic.; see agree), and ut lubet, “as one pleases” (Plaut. Mil. 3.1.111: animō ut lubet, Lewis & Short s.v. bene). The phrase as a whole is not in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

sources: Lewis & Short: sum · Lewis & Short: libet
